dimensions.note: Join tokens live only in memory and a caller-named vault key; state and output carry token ID, role and expiry only. mint_join_token refuses before any remote call without a vault service, takes the ID by decoding the create kubeconfig and corroborating it against the role-scoped token list, and invalidates on any doubt, list failure or vault failure; invalidate overwrites the key with a fixed tombstone. ClusterCommandError carries stderr only, never stdout. SSH key is a sensitive vault reference; strict host keys only (insecure_tofu dropped). Live: ps/argv scan on three nodes and locally across every join, drain, detach and failed join found 0 hits for any token value, bearer, secret half or their sha256, and 0 gzip-base64 strings; every minted token was invalidated (create workflow twice, bad-pin join). Residual MEDIUM: an unparseable create output or a failed final tokens-record write leaves that token live on the controller until token_expiry (default 1h), held nowhere else.
One info line per mint (role, token ID, cluster, expiry); no token value, kubeconfig or host key in log fields or errors.

Typed errors: ClusterCommandError (argv head, exit, trimmed stderr), TokenError, VaultUnavailableError, DetachRefusedError, DrainBlockedError (PDB block, node stays cordoned; live cell 5), WaitTimeoutError. hasNonDaemonSetPods throws on a non-List and detach turns it into a refusal (fails closed). Canonical ssh.ts maps exit 255 to a typed transport error.

29 offline tests: planner (create, HA, even-count, duplicates, upgrade order, quorum and last-controller refusals), token decode and corroboration, argv builders, vault refusals, drain PDB block, detach refusals, sync drift persisted to status, worker role/version from the real k0s 1.36 worker Node shape, workflow structure. Round 3 ran 13 mock workflow cases, every token invalidated. Live: 11 of 12 on 3c8afc1 (3 nodes: one controller, two workers; published k0s-cluster 2026.10.17.3), the one FAIL (sync drift unobservable) and the role residual fixed in f94659f, then 5 of 5 on f94659f. Untested: HA with 3 controllers (quorum paths unit-tested only).

invalidate by key is a no-op once every record is invalidated (live, no remote call); detach of an absent node is a no-op and an already-left etcd member is accepted; drain and uncordon are idempotent. The join-node child workflow pairs every mint with an invalidate (wait completed, or install failed). Workers are gated on the whole controllers job succeeding. Residuals: forEach has no early stop inside a job; an explicit invalidate of an already-invalidated token_id fails when k0s reports it unknown; a re-run mint creates another token.

k0s v1.36.4 checked in a container and live: token create prints a base64 gzipped kubeconfig; token list requires a role; etcd member-list maps name to peer URL; worker Nodes carry no node.k0sproject.io role or version label, so role comes from etcd membership or a ControlNode and the version falls back to the kubelet string. kubectl drain honors PodDisruptionBudgets (never --disable-eviction).

One SSH exec per command through a controller; no remote temp files; polling loops are bounded by timeout_s. Residual (k0s itself): reset leaves /opt/cni/bin, an empty /etc/cni/net.d and a stale kubelet device-plugin socket on workers.

Manifest @randybias/k0s-multinode 2026.10.17.1, Apache-2.0, additionalFiles README.md and LICENSE.txt, two workflows (create-cluster, join-node) named <ext>-<verb>-<object>. Release stanza visibility public, audience general; the five naming answers are in the LOGBOOK, and the name disambiguates from the per-node k0s-cluster. detach_node is DESTRUCTIVE; get, sync, wait_joined, plan and plan_remove are READ-ONLY. Vendored _lib/ssh.ts (fe0139f0) and transport.ts are byte-identical to k0s-cluster. Leak scan, gitleaks and fixture guard pass; history carries only RFC 5737 addresses; live receipts in the LOGBOOK use redacted hosts. Prior art at merge: none for k0s multi-node (Talos and k3s packages are other distributions).

Arguments and resource schemas are strict; node names use the DNS-1123 subdomain grammar before any remote call (live 7b: '-l x=y' refused with 0 remote calls); token IDs ^[a-z0-9]{6}$ (a leading-dash ID is refused); token expiry bounded 5m to 24h; external_lb/cplb_vip require external_address. Read-backs (nodes, etcd, token list) are projected, not strict-parsed. Residual MEDIUM: the workflows' control_plane_load_balancing input is an open object passed to k0s-cluster, which validates it; nested input defaults are not applied by swamp, so callers pass nested fields explicitly.

plan/plan_remove (compute and record), mint/invalidate join tokens, wait_joined, drain/uncordon, detach_node (an action, never kind delete), get and sync. Deferred and recorded: render_config, the upgrade method, and the add-node, remove-node, upgrade-cluster and reset-cluster workflows; per-node install and reset are k0s-cluster's.

Mint refuses without a vault before any remote call. Detach refuses an undrained node or one with schedulable pods, the last controller (even with confirm; live 7a), a 3->2 or 2->1 controller removal without confirm, a peer_address that is not the member's, a worker that is an etcd member, and detaching through the leaving controller's own host. Each destructive method enforces its own preconditions, not only a workflow gate. Residual MEDIUM: the self-host check compares the etcd peer with the ssh.host string only, so a hostname or alternate interface is not caught (quorum and last-controller refusals still apply).
<cluster> (plan), <cluster>-status, <cluster>-tokens; cluster_name is a label grammar, so no '/', '..', '\' or NUL.

Reads only this model's own plan and tokens records via readResource keyed by instance name; the SSH target, key and vault keys arrive as arguments; the vault is used through context.vaultService get/put (object shape, exercised by a plain-object test context).
First release: upgrades[] is a literal empty array; no stored data to migrate.
